methodology: Articles sourced from Virginia-specific RSS feeds and Google News RSS, filtered for AI/technology/workforce relevance, then assessed by Claude against the scenario framework. Each article is tagged with the region it most affects and the scenario it signals toward.

signals.title: Norfolk native brings free AI workshops to Hampton Roads to close the technology gap - WTKR
signals.signal_reading: Free AI workshops targeting Hampton Roads residents directly counter concentration dynamics by building grassroots capability in a non-metro hub region, signaling potential for peer-to-peer knowledge distribution outside traditional tech corridors.

signals.title: Roanoke College launches WorkAI Lab to prepare leaders for new era of technology - Roanoke College
signals.signal_reading: A WorkAI Lab at Roanoke College in Appalachian Virginia creates institutional infrastructure for deep AI leadership development outside NoVA/Richmond, potentially catalyzing distributed capability in a historically underserved region.

signals.title: TAYLOR: AI data centers increase Virginia’s urban-rural divide - The Cavalier Daily
signals.signal_reading: Student editorial explicitly names AI data centers asDriverError of urban-rural divide, signaling that current infrastructure investment patterns are concentrating economic benefits while distributing environmental costs, deepening rather than bridging regional gaps.

signals.title: Virginia needs more technical workers, but it’s stepping away from funding a program to develop them
signals.signal_reading: Defunding GO TEC technical workforce program serving 49 school divisions (many rural) while AI demand surges signals state policy failure to build distributed capability infrastructure precisely when transition support is most critical.

signals.title: Virginia job market faces AI challenge: high-achieving college grads ‘having trouble getting jobs’ - The Virginian-Pilot
signals.signal_reading: High-achieving college graduates struggling to find jobs despite AI boom suggests platforms are automating entry-level work faster than creating new roles, pointing toward shallow adoption that compresses rather than expands the skills ladder.
